$schema_note: THETA Strategy DNA hypothesis registry. Each entry converts an expert-behavior prior into a testable conditional statement, not a hard-coded rule. 'status' is one of RETAIN (already structurally enforced by a TRD [MUST] requirement and/or a non-negotiable rule -- kept as a standing constraint, though still worth confirmatory benchmarking) / CORRECT (the underlying idea is right but needs modification before it is testable or usable as stated) / TEST (open question, needs OOS evidence before promotion either way) / REJECT (should not be pursued). No hypothesis here has been run against real data -- no performance numbers are recorded, and none should be added until an actual backtest produces them (Phase 6, docs/PHASED_PLAN.md).
shared_evidence_requirement: Per TRD v1.1 FINAL section 50: report raw N and independent-cluster N together; a claim approaching the 70-80% headline range needs ~300+ independent OOS episodes, preferably 500+ across regimes, plus a Wilson interval (simple proportions) or cluster/bootstrap interval (dependent episodes). The final untouched OOS period is never used to select the threshold or feature that produced the reported number (ML-002).
shared_calibration_requirement: Per TRD MODEL-003: any model output (not a hand-built deterministic score) feeding this hypothesis must be calibrated (Brier score, log-loss, reliability plot) and monitored by regime/DTE/delta/ticker-family cohort, not by one global number.

hypotheses.statement: Among CSP candidates with similar annualized premium, higher ownership_acceptability and lower p_severe_drawdown is associated with higher Managed Episode WR and lower Whole-Chain drawdown than selecting by premium/IV rank alone.
hypotheses.mechanism: Premium alone cannot distinguish 'volatile but structurally fine to own' from 'richly priced because genuinely fragile'. Screening for ownership quality should reduce the tail cost paid when assignment happens, raising after-cost EV per unit of tail risk taken rather than merely raising the premium collected.
hypotheses.label_definition: Managed-episode after-cost outcome under the fixed training policy/version (TRD section 46), not simple expiry ITM/OTM.
hypotheses.payoff_target: Managed Episode after-cost P&L, always reported alongside Whole-Chain P&L and Open MTM -- never Leg WR alone.
hypotheses.failure_mode: Look-ahead leakage if ownership_acceptability is computed from data unavailable at decision time; survivorship bias if the universe excludes names that later became unacceptable; regime concentration if the test window lacks a real drawdown regime to actually test the tail-cost claim.
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: See shared_calibration_requirement -- applies in full if ownership_acceptability/p_severe_drawdown are model outputs rather than hand-built scores.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: A1 (ownership-augmented selection) beats BQ-1 (premium/IV-rank-only) on untouched-OOS EV_net with an interval excluding zero, without worse DD/ES, across at least two distinct volatility regimes.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: A1 does not beat BQ-1 on after-cost EV_net in untouched OOS, or the improvement vanishes under clustered-bootstrap/regime resampling, or the result required selecting a threshold on the final OOS period.
hypotheses.rationale: Structurally supported by TRD UNIV-001..003 and section 43's ownership model, and is exactly what ablation A1 (B1 + ownership model) already exists to measure -- but it has not been run, so it stays TEST rather than RETAIN.

hypotheses.statement: Selecting CSP candidates by IV rank/percentile alone, without ownership-quality and event-state screening, produces materially worse Whole-Chain WR and higher assignment-drawdown than the same universe filtered by ownership_acceptability.
hypotheses.mechanism: High IV frequently reflects genuine downside/event risk, not a mispriced opportunity; an IV-rank-only filter has no way to tell the two apart, so it systematically selects some names whose premium richness is compensation for real tail risk rather than a discount.

state.volatility: HIGH preferentially selected by the naive filter
state.event_state: any -- this is exactly what an IV-only filter fails to screen

hypotheses.label_definition: Same as H-Q-01 -- managed-episode after-cost outcome, compared between the two selection policies on the same universe/period.
hypotheses.payoff_target: Whole-Chain WR and assignment-drawdown specifically (this hypothesis is about what the naive filter hides, not just EV).
hypotheses.failure_mode: If the two policies are tested on different universes or periods the comparison is meaningless; must hold the candidate universe and time window fixed and vary only the selection rule.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: A1 (ownership-augmented) shows materially better Whole-Chain WR and lower assignment-drawdown than BQ-1 (IV-rank-only) on the identical candidate set/period, with the gap surviving clustered-bootstrap resampling.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: No material difference in Whole-Chain WR/assignment-drawdown between BQ-1 and A1 once compared on the same universe/period, or the apparent gap is an artifact of comparing different underlying sets.
hypotheses.rationale: TRD UNIV-002 already forbids 'high IV alone is sufficient' as a hard rule (RETAIN at the architecture level), but the empirical size of the effect is unmeasured -- this hypothesis is the confirmatory measurement of that rule, not a new claim, and stays TEST until A1 is actually run.

hypotheses.statement: On a separately validated, narrow underlying/policy cohort, a 2-5 DTE ATM/near-ATM short-put policy with intentional assignment and a recovery-wait step achieves a higher Managed Episode WR than the same names traded on the conventional 30-60 DTE lattice -- but this does NOT transfer to other tickers or DTE ranges without its own OOS validation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Very short-dated ATM puts collect less premium per trade but decay faster and are re-underwritten more often; on a narrow, well-understood underlying this can raise per-episode hit rate at the cost of higher gamma/gap exposure right at expiration -- the mechanism trades tail risk concentration for frequency, it does not eliminate risk.

state.trend: range-bound or mildly trending preferred (unverified assumption, not asserted as fact)
state.volatility: any, but gap risk dominates at 2-5 DTE
state.event_state: must exclude near-term earnings given ATM gamma exposure
state.liquidity_state: NORMAL, tight spread required given short DTE

hypotheses.label_definition: Managed-episode outcome specific to the 2-5 DTE cohort, resolved through assignment/recovery-wait, not just expiry ITM/OTM.
hypotheses.payoff_target: Managed Episode WR AND Whole-Chain WR together (per H-H-02 -- WR alone is not sufficient evidence for this archetype).
hypotheses.failure_mode: Gamma/gap risk at 2-5 DTE is easy to underestimate in a backtest that uses close-to-close bars instead of intraday/gap-aware pricing; a naive replay can overstate this archetype's WR by missing adverse gap-through-strike scenarios.
hypotheses.evidence_requirement: See shared_evidence_requirement -- and because this cohort is narrow by design, independent-cluster N will be harder to reach than for THETA-Q; do not lower the bar to compensate.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: The 2-5 DTE cohort beats BH-1 (same names, conventional 30-60 DTE) on Managed Episode WR AND does not underperform on Whole-Chain WR/DD, on a gap-aware backtest, with the specific cohort named and independently validated -- not assumed to generalize.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: The apparent WR edge disappears once gap risk is properly modeled, or Whole-Chain WR/DD is materially worse than BH-1, or the cohort's independent-cluster N is too small to support any claim.
hypotheses.regime_scope_note: This hypothesis targets a narrow 2-5 DTE cohort explicitly distinct from THETA-Q's default 30-60 DTE research lattice -- it is a challenger regime, not a contradiction of THETA-Q's hypotheses, which apply outside this cohort.
hypotheses.rationale: TRD itself frames THETA_HOLD_STRIKE as 'research challenger,' explicitly requiring separate OOS validation before promotion -- never assume its reputation transfers.

hypotheses.statement: IWM Hold-the-Strike's high closed-trade win rate does not by itself prove low risk; Whole-Chain WR and Open MTM inventory must be included before this archetype is compared favorably to any other, because intentional, frequent assignment is exactly the pattern where unresolved stock drawdown can hide behind a high leg-level WR.
hypotheses.mechanism: A closed-trade WR only counts legs that have already resolved; a policy that assigns often necessarily carries more open stock inventory at any snapshot in time, and that inventory's unrealized loss does not appear in a leg-level WR calculation at all until it is eventually closed -- so the metric is structurally biased toward looking safer than it is for exactly this archetype.

state.stress_state: any -- this is a measurement discipline, not a market-conditional claim

hypotheses.label_definition: Not an outcome label to predict -- a reporting-completeness check applied to whatever labels/outcomes the archetype already produces.
hypotheses.payoff_target: N/A -- the target here is correct measurement, not an economic payoff.
hypotheses.failure_mode: The failure mode this hypothesis exists to prevent: reporting Leg WR as if it were the whole picture. Guard by construction (OUT-001..004), not by hoping an analyst remembers.
hypotheses.evidence_requirement: N/A -- verified by architecture/reporting-view inspection (does the performance view expose Leg WR, Managed Episode WR, Whole-Chain WR, and Open MTM together?), not by a statistical sample.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: Every performance report and dashboard view for this archetype exposes Leg WR, Managed Episode WR, Whole-Chain WR, and Open MTM together, with no view surfacing Leg WR alone as a headline.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: N/A -- this is retained by construction; the only 'rejection' would be discovering a reporting view that violates it, which is a bug to fix, not a hypothesis to abandon.
hypotheses.rationale: Already structurally enforced by TRD OUT-001..004 (report Leg WR, Managed Episode WR, Whole-Chain WR and Open MTM together). This is a standing reporting constraint applied specifically to this archetype, not an open statistical question -- no experiment_id because its 'test' is an architecture/reporting check, not an OOS run.

hypotheses.statement: Actively closing or rolling short options before expiration (e.g. near a fixed profit-capture percentage or DTE threshold) produces superior after-cost, capital-day-adjusted returns compared to holding to expiration, in at least some regimes.
hypotheses.mechanism: Most of an option's extrinsic value decays in the final stretch before expiration while gamma/gap risk rises; closing early locks in the bulk of the captured premium and frees capital (redeployable to a new episode) before the highest-risk, lowest-remaining-reward part of the position's life.

state.volatility: elevated volatility regimes plausibly favor early close (unverified)
state.liquidity_state: NORMAL, needed to close/roll without excess slippage

hypotheses.label_definition: Action value comparison at decision time for HOLD/CLOSE/ROLL (TRD section 46) -- not simply whether the position was eventually profitable.
hypotheses.payoff_target: Capital-day-adjusted after-cost EV (ReturnPerCapitalDay), since the mechanism's claimed advantage is capital efficiency, not just terminal P&L.
hypotheses.failure_mode: Comparing CLOSE/ROLL against HOLD using different candidate sets or periods than H-R-02's comparison would make the two hypotheses' results incomparable, defeating the point of preserving them as a real head-to-head. Must share candidate set and period with EXP-R-02.
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: See shared_calibration_requirement -- applies to any fill-probability or capital-day model used to compute the early-close/roll variant's realized economics.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: Active close/roll (BR-1 alternative) beats always-hold (BR-1 baseline) on capital-day-adjusted after-cost EV within A5, on the same candidate set/period used for H-R-02, in at least one clearly named regime.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Active close/roll does not beat always-hold on capital-day-adjusted EV in any regime once transaction costs are included, or the effect is not distinguishable from H-R-02's opposing result on the same data.
hypotheses.rationale: Directly contradicts H-R-02's patience thesis. Both are corpus-supported by different experts and both stay open -- TRD's own failure-DNA table explicitly rejects both 'roll every loser' and a universal hold-to-expiry assumption, so resolving this by averaging the two experts' behavior would manufacture a compromise neither actually demonstrated. The correct resolution is regime/DTE/branch-conditional, decided by A5 (dynamic management ablation) evidence, not by picking a side here.

hypotheses.statement: Holding short options to expiration or full-cycle resolution, rather than closing/rolling early at a fixed profit-capture threshold, produces superior after-cost, capital-day-adjusted returns in at least some regimes, because early close/roll forfeits remaining theta decay and incurs avoidable transaction costs.
hypotheses.mechanism: Closing early realizes a transaction cost (spread/commission) to capture premium that would otherwise continue decaying toward zero for free; if the position was going to expire OTM anyway, closing early is a pure cost with no offsetting benefit -- the patience thesis bets that this is the common case.

state.volatility: low/normal volatility regimes plausibly favor patience (unverified)

hypotheses.label_definition: Same action-value comparison framework as H-R-01 (TRD section 46 management_label), opposing conclusion.
hypotheses.payoff_target: Capital-day-adjusted after-cost EV, same metric as H-R-01 for a fair comparison.
hypotheses.failure_mode: Must share candidate set and period with H-R-01/EXP-R-01 -- see that hypothesis's failure_mode. A subtler risk specific to this side: patience looks better in a backtest that undercounts tail losses from holding through an adverse move, so tail/DD metrics matter as much as average EV here.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: Hold-to-cycle (BR-2 alternative) beats fixed-50%-close/roll (BR-2 baseline) on capital-day-adjusted after-cost EV within A5, on the same candidate set/period used for H-R-01, without worse DD/ES.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Hold-to-cycle does not beat fixed-close/roll on capital-day-adjusted EV once tail risk is accounted for, or DD/ES is materially worse despite a higher average EV.
hypotheses.rationale: See H-R-01 -- this pair is deliberately preserved as competing hypotheses rather than resolved by inspection. TRD Appendix I explicitly frames the 25/50/75% profit-take grid and hold-to-expiry as baselines to test, not laws.

hypotheses.statement: A roll increases after-cost expectancy only when its scenario-EV exceeds the best feasible alternative (close/hold/assign/redeploy) computed at the same decision timestamp; a policy that rolls every moderately-losing short leg underperforms one that explicitly compares roll against alternatives.
hypotheses.mechanism: A roll is close-old plus open-new (TRD section 24) -- it is never free. 'Rolling every loser' spends transaction costs and extends capital lock-up on positions that a genuine alternatives comparison (e.g. accepting assignment, or redeploying to a better candidate) would sometimes reject; requiring the comparison should filter out the negative-EV rolls a naive always-roll policy would take.

state.stress_state: any -- the discipline should hold everywhere, unlike H-R-01/H-R-02's regime-conditional claims

hypotheses.label_definition: Incremental value of new exposure versus best feasible alternative at the same timestamp (TRD section 46).
hypotheses.payoff_target: RollUtility (TRD Appendix A: EV_new - EV_best_alternative - tail/capital-day/opportunity-cost penalties).
hypotheses.failure_mode: The subtle risk here is treating a positive NetRollCredit as proof of a good roll -- TRD explicitly rejects that (Appendix A distinguishes NetRollCredit from RollUtility). A naive test that only checks 'was the roll credit positive' would falsely confirm this hypothesis without ever computing the alternatives comparison it actually claims matters.
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: See shared_calibration_requirement -- applies to any model used to estimate EV_best_alternative.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: A policy that computes RollUtility against all four alternatives before rolling beats a naive always-roll-if-credit-positive policy on after-cost EV_net, in A5, without materially worse DD.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: The alternatives-comparison policy does not beat the naive always-roll policy, or the two are statistically indistinguishable once costs are included -- which would mean the discipline adds no measurable value despite being structurally required.
hypotheses.rationale: Already a hard TRD rule (ROLL-002: roll only when it beats hold/close/assign/redeploy under the same state). RETAIN at the architecture level; still worth an A5 ablation to size how much this discipline is actually worth versus a naive always-roll policy.

hypotheses.statement: Selling covered calls to maximize annualized yield alone underperforms, on a full stock-plus-call lifecycle EV basis, a policy that trades off premium against retained upside and call-away regret -- particularly ahead of known events.
hypotheses.mechanism: Maximum-yield CC selection picks the strike/expiry with the richest premium regardless of how likely or costly a call-away is; if the stock later rallies past that strike, the yield-maximizing choice forfeits upside the stockholder would otherwise have kept, and that forfeited upside is a real economic cost the yield number never shows.

state.trend: upside call-away regret matters most in an uptrending or event-catalyst regime

hypotheses.label_definition: After-cost stock+call utility and call-away outcome conditional on stock state (TRD section 46).
hypotheses.payoff_target: CCUtility (TRD section 23: EV_premium + EV_stock - CallAwayRegret - EventRiskPenalty - ExecutionCost - TailPenalty).
hypotheses.failure_mode: A backtest that only scores realized premium and ignores forfeited upside on called-away shares will structurally favor the yield-maximizing policy regardless of the truth -- CallAwayRegret must actually be computed from the post-call-away stock path, not omitted as too hard to measure.
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: See shared_calibration_requirement -- applies to the covered-call ranker's utility model.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: Full-utility CC selection beats BC-1 (max-yield-only) on CCUtility in untouched OOS, with the gap concentrated in (and explainable by) event-adjacent and uptrending episodes.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: No CCUtility improvement over BC-1, or CallAwayRegret cannot be measured/estimated with acceptable reliability, making the comparison untrustworthy either way.
hypotheses.rationale: Already required by TRD LIFE-004 (the CC optimizer must trade off premium, retained upside, call-away regret, event risk and capital-days, not maximize yield alone). RETAIN at the architecture level; the experiment sizes the effect against BC-1.

hypotheses.statement: Covered calls sold immediately upon every assignment (no recovery wait) underperform, on a full-chain basis, a policy that conditions the CC decision on recovery-thesis state -- e.g. waiting while the stock is significantly underwater relative to basis.
hypotheses.mechanism: Selling a call on stock that just got assigned deep underwater caps upside at a strike that may lock in a loss if called away, before the position has had any chance to recover -- waiting preserves the option to sell a call once the stock is closer to (or above) basis, which is a strictly wider set of choices than being forced to decide the moment assignment happens.

state.trend: underwater relative to assignment basis specifically

hypotheses.label_definition: Same as H-C-01, but specifically conditioned on post-assignment recovery state rather than general CC selection.
hypotheses.payoff_target: Full-chain (stock + eventual CC) after-cost P&L, not the immediate CC premium alone.
hypotheses.failure_mode: A short backtest window can make 'sell CC immediately' look fine simply because the test period didn't include a case where the stock later recovered well past the strike -- needs a period/sample with genuine post-assignment recovery variance to be a fair test.
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: See shared_calibration_requirement -- applies to the recovery-thesis state estimate driving the wait/sell decision.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: Recovery-conditioned CC policy beats BC-2 (immediate CC after every assignment) on full-chain after-cost P&L in untouched OOS, across a sample that includes real post-assignment recovery variance.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: No full-chain improvement over BC-2, or the test sample lacks enough recovery variance to distinguish the two policies meaningfully.
hypotheses.rationale: This is one of the charter's own non-negotiable rules ('do not automatically sell a covered call immediately after every assignment') and TRD STRAT-003. RETAIN at the architecture level; BC-2 exists to confirm the effect empirically, not to decide whether the rule applies.

hypotheses.statement: Assignment, when the underlying remains ownership-acceptable, produces superior full-chain economic outcomes than mechanically closing the CSP for a loss before assignment to avoid holding stock.
hypotheses.mechanism: Closing a CSP for a loss right before assignment realizes that loss in cash and forfeits any chance the underlying recovers; accepting assignment on an ownership-acceptable name converts the same economic exposure into stock that can recover, pay dividends, and later support a covered call -- mechanically closing throws away optionality the corpus's 'patience' priors say is often worth keeping.

state.trend: any, conditioned on ownership_acceptability remaining above the entry-floor threshold
state.stress_state: NORMAL or CORRECTION -- CRISIS-regime assignment is a materially different, untested case

alternatives: CLOSE_STOCK (closing the CSP itself before assignment)
hypotheses.label_definition: Assignment event plus post-assignment downside/recovery path; assignment itself is neither automatic win nor loss (TRD section 46).
hypotheses.payoff_target: Full-chain (CSP + stock + eventual exit) after-cost P&L, compared against the cash-realized-loss-only alternative.
hypotheses.failure_mode: Must not compare 'assignment happened to work out' anecdotes -- needs the full distribution of assignment outcomes including cases where the stock did not recover, or this looks better than it is by survivorship.
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: See shared_calibration_requirement -- applies to the ownership/recovery models gating whether assignment is deemed acceptable in the first place.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: Accept-assignment-when-acceptable beats BA-1 (mechanical close-before-assignment) on full-chain after-cost EV in untouched OOS, and B6 (buy-and-hold assigned underlying) shows THETA's active management adds further value beyond passive holding.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: BA-1 (mechanical close) matches or beats accept-assignment on full-chain EV, or B6 shows THETA's management subtracts value versus simply holding the assigned stock.
hypotheses.rationale: TRD STRAT-002 already treats assignment as a feasible, intentional transition when conditions remain acceptable. RETAIN at the architecture level; B6 (buy-and-hold assigned underlying) provides confirmatory evidence on whether Wheel management specifically adds value post-assignment.

hypotheses.statement: A recovery-wait policy with an explicit risk/time/thesis-invalidation bound produces better outcomes than unconditionally waiting for full recovery to original entry economics -- though the *existence* of such a bound is already a settled design rule; only its specific parameterization (how long, how much invalidation) is genuinely open.
hypotheses.mechanism: Unbounded recovery-wait ties up capital indefinitely on a thesis that may never play out and blocks that capital from being redeployed to a fresh positive-EV episode; a bound forces an explicit comparison between 'keep waiting' and 'redeploy elsewhere', which unconditional waiting never makes.

state.event_state: any -- thesis-invalidating events are exactly what the bound should react to

hypotheses.label_definition: Time-to-approved-recovery or censoring if unresolved at dataset cutoff (TRD section 46) -- open recovery episodes must be censored, not counted as wins or losses.
hypotheses.payoff_target: Capital-days-adjusted after-cost EV, since the core claim is about capital efficiency of a bounded vs. unbounded wait, not just terminal outcome.
hypotheses.failure_mode: As flagged in rationale: this statement conflates a settled rule (a bound should exist) with an open parameter (what the bound is). Testing it as written risks silently picking a threshold and reporting confirmation, which is exactly the kind of parameter-tuning-toward-a-desired-result the charter prohibits -- must be re-split into constraint + parameter sweep before use (see rationale).
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: See shared_calibration_requirement -- applies to the recovery-time survival model (S_recovery(t)) underlying the bound.
hypotheses.evidence_requirement: See shared_evidence_requirement -- plus explicit censoring of unresolved recovery episodes at the dataset cutoff, never counted as wins or losses.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: NOT to be evaluated as a single acceptance test until split into a parameter sweep (see rationale); once split, each candidate threshold is accepted only if it beats BA-2 (unconditional wait) on capital-days-adjusted EV without the threshold having been chosen using the same OOS data used to evaluate it.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Any candidate threshold that does not beat BA-2, or that was selected by looking at the same OOS results used to confirm it (a labeled parameter-tuning violation).
hypotheses.rationale: Marked CORRECT rather than a clean TEST/RETAIN because it conflates two different questions: whether a bound should exist (RETAIN -- already TRD OWN-002) and what the bound's specific threshold should be (TEST, and per the charter this threshold must never be tuned merely to hit a target win rate). Before this hypothesis is used by the backtester it should be split into a settled architectural constraint plus a distinct, explicitly-parameterized TEST hypothesis per candidate threshold -- do not treat the single statement above as backtester-ready as written.

hypotheses.statement: Closed-trade or Leg win rate alone will systematically overstate an assignment-heavy archetype's safety when unresolved assigned-stock losses are excluded from the headline metric; Managed Episode WR, Whole-Chain WR and Open MTM must be reported together for any assignment/recovery-heavy archetype.
hypotheses.mechanism: Same structural bias as H-H-02, restated for THETA-A specifically: assignment/recovery is where open stock inventory accumulates the most, so this is the archetype where the Leg-WR blind spot is largest in absolute terms.
hypotheses.label_definition: Reporting-completeness check, not a predicted outcome label.
hypotheses.payoff_target: N/A -- correct measurement, not an economic payoff.
hypotheses.failure_mode: Same as H-H-02: the failure this exists to prevent is reporting Leg WR as if it were the whole picture, specifically for the archetype most exposed to it.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: THETA-A performance views expose Leg WR, Managed Episode WR, Whole-Chain WR, and Open MTM together, with recovery-wait duration and capital lock-up alongside them.
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: N/A -- retained by construction; a violating report view is a bug, not a falsified hypothesis.
hypotheses.rationale: Structurally enforced by TRD OUT-001..004 already. This is the same cross-cutting failure-DNA constraint recorded in strategy_archetypes.json, restated here specifically for THETA-A where the risk is sharpest, given how central assignment/recovery is to this archetype.

hypotheses.statement: When full cash-secured CSP quantity would be zero (collateral/risk-budget insufficient) or tail risk is poorly bounded, a defined-risk put-credit-spread structure can express the same premium thesis with bounded downside, at the cost of capped upside and typically worse fill/liquidity quality.
hypotheses.mechanism: A cash-secured put's downside is uncapped (bounded only by the strike); buying a further-OTM put against it caps that downside at the cost of some premium and, since the long-put leg trades on a thinner part of the chain, generally worse fill quality -- this trades bounded-but-certain cost against unbounded-but-unlikely cost.

state.liquidity_state: must be checked on BOTH legs, not just the short strike

alternatives: WAIT (if full CSP quantity is zero and no defined-risk alternative exists)
hypotheses.label_definition: Same entry_label framework as THETA-Q, applied to a spread structure instead of a single short put.
hypotheses.payoff_target: After-cost EV per unit of capital at risk, compared against simply not trading when full CSP sizing is unavailable.
hypotheses.failure_mode: Gated (see gated_until) -- premature testing risks consuming research effort on a branch the TRD explicitly says is not ready, and risks a false-positive result influencing THETA-Q/H/R/C/A work it should stay separate from.
hypotheses.calibration_requirement: Not applicable until this archetype is ungated; see shared_calibration_requirement for the general standard it would need to meet.
hypotheses.evidence_requirement: Not applicable until this archetype is ungated; see shared_evidence_requirement for the general standard.
hypotheses.acceptance_criterion: Not to be evaluated before gating conditions are met (see gated_until).
hypotheses.rejection_criterion: Not to be evaluated before gating conditions are met (see gated_until).
hypotheses.candidate_actions_note: The action vocabulary supplied for this registry (WAIT/OPEN_CSP/HOLD/CLOSE/ROLL/ASSIGN/EXPIRE/RECOVERY_WAIT/SELL_CC/CLOSE_STOCK/REDEPLOY) has no distinct action for 'open a defined-risk spread' -- it is CSP/Wheel-centric by design. This is a known vocabulary gap, left unfilled rather than silently inventing a new action, since THETA-D is explicitly deferred.
hypotheses.gated_until: Alpaca options trading Level 3 confirmed AND THETA-Q/H/R/C/A have graduated (see strategy_archetypes.json). Registered for research completeness only -- do not begin implementation.
hypotheses.rationale: TRD section 3.1 explicitly permits this branch only after Level 3 support and separate OOS validation. Recording it now (rather than omitting it) keeps the structure-routing evidence from Ivan Orehovec and Lick Neeson from being silently dropped, while making the gating condition impossible to miss.
